[quote=shahban;60993336][b]Press Statement from High Emir Rashad al-Hawrin in Qarandah[/b]

We formally demands compensation from Greater [nation]Tirakan[/nation] for losses incurred as a direct result of unreasoned enhanced customs controls, administrative obstruction, and the unlawful placement of Shahbani-owned assets under state administration.
These actions have caused measurable financial damage to Shahbani enterprises and undermined contractual obligations without due process or international mandate. Such measures cannot be dismissed as precautionary anymore.

Based on preliminary assessments conducted by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Trade, Shahban estimates direct and indirect damages to exceed 12.8 billion Ran [i](11.13 billion $)[/i], including seized assets, interrupted operations, contractual penalties, and logistical losses. We therefore call upon Greater Tirakan to immediately establish a framework for compensation commensurate with the harm caused.
Should these matters remain unresolved, Shahban will pursue all available legal and diplomatic avenues to protect the rights of its citizens and enterprises.

Shahban reiterates that it does not seek escalation. However, responsibility for addressing the consequences of recent actions rests with those who implemented them.

An eye for an eye.

[i](The Emir leaves the podium without taking any questions)[/i][/quote]

[b]Naerim, Statement from the Office of Foreign Affairs[/b]

Greater Tirakan categorically rejects Shahban's demand for compensation.

No obligation exists under international law or bilateral agreement that would require Greater Tirakan to provide recompensation for lawful administrative measures taken within its own jurisdiction.  Greater Tirakan does not accept responsibility for commercial losses arising from Shahbans own policy decisions, risk exposure, or escalation of rhetoric. Claims of any unlawful administrations are without proof and will not be acknowledged as a basis for compensation.

Accordingly, no compensation will be paid.

Greater Tirakan remains open to dialogue conducted in good faith. However, demands framed as ultimatums do not advance resolution. The responsibility for de-escalation rests within all of us.

[spoiler=Regional stability above all.][b]Official statement from the Valdderan Government[/b]

The Government of Valddera and Supreme leader Osman Rayad formally invites the two neighboring countries of [nation]Shahban[/nation] and [nation]Tirakan[/nation] for peace talks due to their recent trade dispute and other situations, Valddera emphasizes that this initiative is undertaken in the interest of continental stability, freedom of commerce, and the prevention of escalation that could undermine regional security. The talks will be hosted at Valddera's capital, Vald. under Valdderan security guarantees, with the sole objective of facilitating dialogue and mutually acceptable solutions, Valddera does not seek to impose outcomes, but to ensure that disagreements and tensions are resolved through negotiation rather than disruption or conflict.

By that, Valddera offers those mutual agreements to both sides. Valddera will let Shahban have a port in the country under state protection, a port from the southern coastal city in mainland Valddera, the trading hub and economic city of Serene, considering that they are a land-locked country. Valddera also proposes for mutual businesses to flow smoothly through Shahban and Valddera, Valddera also demands for the stolen goods and facilites under Tiraki state administration to be returned back to Shahban as a part of the agreement, and also encourages for both nations to have economic ties. This also follows the proposed deals and agreements from Tirakan:
Tirakan pays no compensation.

Tirakan gives no admission of wrongdoing.

Tirakan will immediately return all Shahbani assets, without the inspections.

Shahban recieves a treaty port in Valddera.

Shahban will be granted enhanced access to Tiraki ports.

No lithium extraction on Shahbani territory anymore.

A free trade agreement is signed, abolishing all tariffs between Shahban and Tirakan.

Shahban will fully restore civilian aviation and overflight rights.

Shahban will formally retract all public warnings and threats.

Shahban and Tirakan sign a NAP.

Shahban aligns and joins the SSP.

Shahban commits to non-alignment with shamat-external power blocs.

Tirakan guarantees Shahbans sovereignty and vice versa.

Tirakan finances new pipelines, energy grids and logistic corridors in Shahban.

Tirakan guarantees to cover Shahbans energy demand with Tiraki-priced gas.

Tiraki development banks finance Shahbani state funds and private loans.

Shahban's logistics will be standardized to Tiraki norm, to ensure future Tiraki logistic services in Shahban.[/spoiler]

[b]By the River[/b]

Elena and Cecilia finished their meals with lively chatter. The afternoon gave way to twilight, the purple sky reflected on the slow-moving river by the restaurant. The couple traded affectionate, lingering touches and strolled out into the night. Elena led the way through a forest path down to the riverwalk. It was a warm, spring evening filled with fireflies and chirping crickets. Old fashioned lightposts colored the night in a warm, soft yellow. Elena bent down and picked a small flower from the grass, kissing it and offering it to her partner.

[i]A flower, for my sweet, sweet blossom. Tomorrow the Palace staff with be hosting a feast and dance, a part of our spring festival. Would you like to come with? Some friends will be in town, and theyre planning an after party.[/i]

She put an arm around Cecilias back and kissed her forehead, [i]And Id love to share a dance with you.[/i]

[quote=greater_rostoria;60989895]The Maglev swiftly transported the men towards the local administrative office, a large brutalist building covered in the flags of Korrin, the Red Sun contrasting heavily with the white exterior of the infrastructure. Joseph was ushered to Cargillis' office and was seated at a large red cushioned chair lined with intricately detailed gold, with the desk being made from imported redwood. A half full glass of whiskey was sitting near the edge of the table and from brief glimpses Joseph could spot documents detailing military production before they were swept away into a drawer.

Cargillis sat down opposite of Joseph, with the four naval officers following the men into the room and standing just a few feet from Joseph. Cargillis brushed the desk for any dust and took a quick sip from the glass, he locked his hands together and pressed down on the table. [i]"Well, mister Joseph, I'm sure you're a busy man with many things to attend to so I won't drag this meeting out, let's get it over quick."[/i] Cargillis paused for a moment and gazed at Joseph to see his reaction.

[i]"I know Rosenmarkke and the rest of Erene are suffering heavily due to this wave of revolutions, and while the rest of the Federation has taken a militaristic approach, your nation has been smart enough to recognise that peace with the Spacenoids is the only way to save an economy. You need resources, Miosul is too much of a hassle to properly exploit, and thus the only reliable stream of metals and such has to come from beyond the belt.

Korrin can provide it, though we won't be sending you our trade ships while the war is happening, you'll have to send us your ships if you want the resources. And in exchange Korrin wants nothing more than cheap food, cheapest as could be. Doesn't matter how bad it tastes, as long as there is enough being sent to us to keep our people alive. The damn Federation tried starving us all in hopes we'd crawl back to them, but luckily Rosenmarkke is truly a noble state."[/i][/quote]

Joseph listened for a moment before replying, 

[i]"I will note that our support of your state is not solely one sided, you see by supporting you we are more than likely to draw the ire of the most loyal Erenite states, we have exposed ourselves to a high risk, high volatility scenario with our decision to recognise you,"[/i] he paused, [i]"It is thus necessary that we should lay out our expectations, our conditions for our deal, firstly you will not attack Rosenmarkke in the event of a war and secondly you and your allies will recognise whatever Vespurian emperor we place on the throne of what remains of Erene bound Vespurias."[/i]

The borders of Hayan-Dal had been shrunk from the former glorious state. This was a grave transgression against the faithful people of the nation.

General Secretary Jin Taeja grimaced. He had only taken power around two weeks ago, and although he had many plans, there wasnt that much he could do with the current state of the nation. He stood from his desk at the Seong, the highest governmental building in all of Hayan-Dal, and took a walk through the halls. He did this to clear his mind, but it was futile; he just kept thinking of ways to improve the situation of the nation.

He turned left at the hallway intersection and walked past two wooden doors. At the third, he gently rested his hand on its bronze handle. He almost turned back. Taeja turned the knob and entered.

The room he entered had twelve pews, six on each side. He walked on the scarlet carpet stretching from the entryway to the altar. At the front, behind the ornate altar, was a large golden crucifix. Taeja read the inscription at the top of the cross.

[i][pre]    IESUS NAZARENUS REX IUDAEORUM[/pre][/i]

Taeja knelt on one knee before the altar. He held the silver cross that hung around his neck with his right hand, and a few quiet moments passed. Finally, he closed his eyes.

[i]Heavenly Father,[/i] he began, [i]Lord of Hosts. Your name is holy above all others, sanctified in a world of impurity. Only Yours is the glory, and only Yours is the power.[/i]

He paused. [i]God, Ive come to ask you for guidance. I desire to grow the borders of our nation, to build up our strength, and yet there seems to be no good avenue through which it could be done. I need your help, just an idea.[/i]

Taeja looked up from his reflective posture about to speak once more, until the image of the Savior struck him. Taeja had been searching for a worldly solution to solve worldly issues, but he had neglected the answer that lied before him. Taeja forgot, [i]He[/i] is the truth, the solution to the issues anyone would face.

The General Secretary lowered his head once more. [i]I thank You, king of kings. You are wise and powerful beyond measure; I ask that You bestow your power and grace upon me, let me do Your on this earth. In the name of Christ, Amen.[/i]

Taeja stood slowly and in reverence. He tucked the silver cross around his neck beneath his gray shirts collar, turned, and left.

[spoiler=
[pre]Movement from the Heavens[/pre]]

The morning sun sat low on the horizon. Thousands gathered under the Seongs balcony, ready to hear the words of the General Secretary.

Taeja, meanwhile, paced through the halls. He wore a gray commanders outfit: a soldiers coat with decorations pinned onto it on top of a gray shirt and tie, dark gray pants, and black boots. It had been a week since the prayer that inspired him to take this course of action. He would be lying if he said that he wasnt nervous in the slightest bit, but he knew that this was meant to be. Taeja knew he was chosen.

He turned sharply towards the hall that took him to the balcony, and with one grand motion, opened the double wooden doors. At his appearance, the people below cheered.

The General Secretary walked towards the podium prepared and tapped the microphone twice. He waited until the people had quieted down to begin speaking. [i]Greetings, people of Hayan-Dal. It is such a fine morning, I hope you all are well.[/i]

He paused for a short while. [i]I come here to speak to you about a great issue that plagues our nation. That is, the one of faith.[/i] The crowd grew even more quiet and still. Taeja continued. [i]We are silent in a time when this godless world needs to hear the Word. We are isolated when we should be reaching out. We, as a nation, are doing good, but as Gods prophets, we are failing.[/i]

He paused for a little while. [i]This is not a problem without remedy, however. This is something that we can all do to fix this. First, we must initiate programs to help our brothers and sisters who fall behind. I already have drafts of these programs sitting on my desk. Secondly, we increase our industrial capacity. This will give us more wealth and resources, and finally allow us to look outwards with more serious intentions. And then-![/i] He raised his fist. [i]And then, we push our borders! We take more land, dedicating yet another part of this world to God. We must spread the faith, and grow our power. We need to strengthen the nation in order to remain faithful. After all, faith without works is dead. And it is in our best interest to remain alive in Him.[/i]

The people below Taeja cheered loudly. He let their praises lift themselves high to him. Looking over the crows, he couldnt help but smile; this was surely the work of God.

[i]After the nation is ready,[/i] he began again after the cheering had died down, [i]I will assemble a group of some faithful few to help with some tasks related to this. But now, we must remember this: the will of God has set our destiny before us like a fruit hanging from a tree. All we must do is reach forth and pluck the fruit, take our destiny.[/i]

Taeja looked over the crowd as they began to cheer again, and after a few minutes, he turned back into the Seong.
[/spoiler]
